To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Keller-Mikses equation is used to model bubble dynamics in a linear viscolelastic medium, and the effects of compressibility and viscoelastic properties on the bubble dynamics are investigated.

the oscillation period, minimum bubble radius, and damping coefficient are strongly dependent on the visco-elastic properties, and the damping coefficient has a non-monotonic dependence on the elasticity.

(1) the oscillation frequency of the bubble in viscoelastic tissue is lower than that in a purely viscous medium; (2) the damping decreases with increasing elasticity and viscosity, but increases with increasing relaxation time; (3) there exists a finite elasticity for which the bubble has the minimum damping; and (4) the period of oscillation generally changes with time, before reaching an asymptotic value.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of a gas bubble undergoing nonlinear oscillations in a viscoelastictissue.
the dynamics of a gas bubble undergoing Rayleigh collapse in a visco-elastic medium.
the Rayleigh collapse, subsequent oscillations, and nonlinear dynamics of a gas bubble within a linear visco-elastic (tissue like) medium.

viscoelasticity has a significant impact on the bubble dynamics, which is especially pronounced when elasticity is small, and the Keller-Miksys equation should be used when the oscillation amplitude is large.
the viscoelasticity and compressibility of the medium have a significant effect on the bubble dynamics.
the viscoelastic material properties of tissue significantly influence the bubble dynamics.

the viscoelasticity of soft tissue has a strong effect on the oscillations following the collapse of a gas-filled microbubble.
the Keller-Miksiss equation for a gas bubble in viscoelastic media is a useful and accurate tool for predicting bubble dynamics in soft tissues.
we have provided a theoretical and numerical framework to study the Rayliegh collapse and subsequent oscillation of gas bubbles in a visco-elastic material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Rayleigh collapse in tissue is not a simple, single event but rather a complex, nonlinear process that depends on both the tissue and bubble properties.
tissue elasticity and compressibility play a significant role in bubble dynamics.
the bubble dynamics are highly nonlinear and depend strongly on the compressibility of the liquid and the viscoelasticity of the surrounding medium.
